what_happened: Research found the repo already has a precedent idiom (task-ref-ok, version-ok inline/block substring markers) structurally identical to what this task needs, plus a rendered-style example (founder/commands/consult.md:22) proving the exact markdown form works. No new mechanism design was needed, only applying the existing idiom to a new lint.

Research recommended applying the new marker to the two /ide lines in memory-setup.md and memory-troubleshooting.md as part of this task, but the dispatch SCOPE BOUNDARY and task 512's own file_scope (lint + test suite only) forbid it; those docs are owned by reword_dead_lifecycle_command_prose_per_class. Plan delivers the mechanism only and records the exact marker string in the lint header for that record's implementer; gate 24 therefore stays red on those two lines after 512 completes.

Discovered during planning that gate24_run invokes the SOURCE-STORE lint directly while the test suite's common_test_resolve_candidate prefers the DEPLOYED copy -- an asymmetry the research report did not cover. Catching it at plan time turned a would-be mid-implementation red suite into a deliberate, documented phase ordering (source-store fixture checks in phases 1-2, redeploy in phase 3).
